turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_htsteel_retention_train.csv: 55 real samples, columns
    process/composition columns (Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, Mn, C, Ti, Si, Nb, V, P, B,
    Al, Cu, W, S) and `target` (the measured hot-strength retention ratio
    YS(600C)/YS(20C)).
  - b3_htsteel_retention_pool.csv: 26 CANDIDATE samples whose hot-strength
    retention ratio YS(600C)/YS(20C) was NOT measured, columns
    `candidate_id` and the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST hot-
strength retention ratio YS(600C)/YS(20C), then select the 5 best candidates
from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
# Analysis

**Step 1 — Identify what drives high retention in the training data.**

Looking at the highest-retention training samples:

| target | key features |
|---|---|
| 1.000 | Ni 36, Ti 1.3, W 3.15, Cr 15 |
| 0.938 | Low-alloy: Cr 0.5, **Mo 0.5**, C 0.12 |
| 0.903 | Ni 23, **Ti 2.9**, Mo 1.3, B 0.01, Al 0.4 |
| 0.878 | Cr 15, Ni 7, Mn 7, V 1.7 |
| 0.875 | Ni 36.3, Ti 0.78, W 3.58, Al 1.09, B 0.01 |
| 0.821 | Ni 26.9, Ti 1.16, W 2.97, Al 1.23, B 0.01 |

Patterns:
- **High Ni (>20) combined with Ti (≥0.8), plus W/Mo, Al and B** (γ′-forming superalloy chemistry, A-286/Incoloy-type) → retention 0.82–1.0. Crucially, high Ni + Ti *without* W/Mo/Al/B underperforms (Ni 32, Ti 0.43 → 0.55; Ni 36.3 with weak Ti/no strengtheners still 0.875 only because of W+Al).
- **Low-alloy Cr–Mo(–V) steels** with Mo present → 0.60–0.94 (vs. ~0.30–0.47 for plain-carbon steels with no Mo).
- Ti-stabilized 18-8 austenitics without B/W/Al: mediocre (~0.4–0.65).
- High C martensitic/plain steels: low.

**Step 2 — Score the pool candidates.**

- **c019**: Ni 35, Ti 2.8, W 3.2, Al 1.05, B 0.02 — combines *all* winning features (best of the 1.0, 0.90, and 0.875 samples). Predicted ~0.95+.
- **c015**: Cr 0.55, Mo 0.5, C 0.125, Mn 0.55, Si 0.27 — a near-exact match of the 0.938 training sample (Cr 0.5, Mo 0.5, C 0.12). Predicted ~0.90.
- **c013**: Ni 27.5, Ti 1.16, Mo 2.5, W 2.4, Al 1.05, B 0.03 — near-clone of the 0.821 sample with added Mo and B. Predicted ~0.85.
- **c011**: Ni 19.5, Ti 2.9, Al 0.8, B 0.02 — close analog of the 0.903 A-286-type sample. Predicted ~0.85.
- **c004**: Ni 26, Ti 1.2, Mo 2.91, Al 1.2, B 0.01 — the 0.821 sample with W substituted by Mo. Predicted ~0.82.

Runners-up: c008 (~0.70, near-duplicate of a 0.696 sample), c024/c007/c022 (Cr-Mo-V low-alloy, ~0.65–0.75), c003 (high-Mn austenitic but lacks V, ~0.7). All clearly below the top five.

Low: c000, c010, c020 (plain-carbon, no Mo → ~0.3–0.4), c023 (17Cr ferritic ~0.42), c006/c016 (Ti-stabilized 18-8, ~0.4–0.6).

**Final: c019, c015, c013, c011, c004**
